title: unified-hydrator-pydantic-dataclass-stream-playbook
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Problem: customers building streaming LLM flows get inconsistent typed outputs when responses arrive incrementally, or when retries/fallbacks replay partial chunks. Existing hydrator adapters either force pydantic-first (heavy runtime) or dataclass-first (lighter but missing runtime validation) which complicates backoff/retry semantics for idempotent vs non-idempotent requests. Goal: design and ship a unified 'hydrator' playbook that provides: 1) safe, incremental construction of typed models (pydantic and dataclass-compatible) from stream chunks; 2) deterministic idempotency markers and checkpointing for retry/fallback; 3) ergonomic helpers for library users (cookbook examples) that show migration paths; 4) tests and benchmarks proving <10% overhead vs current streaming parser for typical chat generation workloads. Acceptance criteria: - New hydrator API with clear migration example in README - Streaming parser supports partial-validation mode and final-strict validation mode - Retry checkpoint protocol that integrates with the SDK's retry middleware and exposes per-request checkpoint tokens to the app - Backcompat: existing typed-helpers continue to work with minimal adapter shim - Unit & integration tests added; performance tests demonstrating N tokens/sec and memory footprint numbers in CI.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: reviewed trade-offs between pydantic-first and dataclass-first approaches. Decided on hybrid adapter pattern: prefer lightweight dataclass construction during stream, run final strict pydantic validation at stream completion or at checkpoints.
2026-03-05 - Prototype: implemented stream-safe field accumulation and incremental union resolution. Early microbench shows ~6% CPU overhead for 1k token streams compared to baseline parser.

2026-03-09 - Design review with PM/Docs: agreed to include 3 cookbook patterns: 'optimistic dataclass' (low-latency), 'strict pydantic' (validation-on-completion), and 'checkpointed replay' (idempotent retries). PM requested explicit sample for function/tool-calling outputs.
2026-03-11 - Security note: encryption/KMS not directly impacted; flagged for security review if we add persisted checkpoint tokens (TBD).
2026-03-13 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/1287. Requesting review from @maria and @sunil for retry middleware integration.
2026-03-14 - Blocker: found an edge case where union-type fields with late-disambiguation cause repeated validation churn; working on memoized resolution to avoid repeated pydantic parsing.

test_plan: Unit tests covering incremental construction, union disambiguation, and final validation. Integration tests using real model streaming fixtures to assert checkpoint tokens enable exact replay semantics. Perf tests run in CI comparing token throughput and peak memory before/after. Add fuzz tests for fragmented JSON chunks in streams.
qa_checklist: Can construct typed model incrementally without triggering full validation on every chunk
Checkpoint tokens allow retry middleware to resume from last acknowledged token
Final strict mode rejects invalid outputs and surfaces clear error messages
Migration example converts an existing pydantic-first consumer to the optimistic dataclass pattern
Performance regression <10% for typical chat workloads in benchmark dashboard
implementation_notes: Proposed API: Hydrator = HydratorFactory.for_model(MyModel, mode="optimistic"|"strict"|"checkpointed"). Hydrator exposes .feed(chunk) -> list[events] and .checkpoint() -> token. Internally use dataclass factory + lazy pydantic.BaseModel.parse_obj at checkpoint. Memoize union resolutions using a small LRU keyed by field-path and recent discriminator tokens to avoid repeated heavy parsing. Expose context manager to bind hydrator lifecycle to request retry scope.
open_questions: Should checkpoint tokens be opaque UUIDs or structured (offset + hash)?
Do we persist checkpoint tokens in local disk for long-running streams (e.g., uploads) or keep ephemeral only?
What's the SDK contract for non-idempotent model calls when a retry occurs mid-stream? Should SDK always surface an explicit 'retry not safe' exception?
